q: A message says you must act in 5 minutes or lose your account. What should you do first?
options: Pause and verify through an official channel
why: Urgency is a common social-engineering pressure. Slow down and verify independently.

q: Someone you met in a game asks for your real school name and home location. What is safer?
options: Do not share it and tell a trusted adult
why: Children should avoid sharing real-world identifying details with unknown people online.

q: Which setting helps reduce who can see your social-media posts?
why: Private settings can limit exposure, although they do not make content risk-free.

q: You receive a free-game-skin link from an unknown account. What is the safest response?
options: Check the official game site and avoid unknown downloads
why: Free-item bait can be used to deliver malware or steal credentials.

q: A message claims to be a campus recruiter and asks for a payment to release an internship offer. What should you do?
options: Verify the recruiter through official college/company channels
why: Independent verification is safer than trusting an urgent payment request.

q: Your manager appears to request an urgent bank transfer by voice message. What should you do?
options: Verify using a known phone number or established process
why: Voice cloning and impersonation can make fake requests sound convincing; verify through an independent channel.

q: A caller says your computer has a virus and demands gift cards to fix it. What is safer?
options: Hang up and contact a trusted person or official support number
why: Urgent gift-card payment demands are a strong scam warning sign.

q: A child tells you they were bullied online. What first response is most helpful?
options: Listen calmly, save evidence and plan the next safe step
why: A calm response encourages reporting and helps preserve useful evidence.

q: Which is a safer rule for multiplayer games?
options: Do not share passwords or real-world location
why: Gaming accounts and chats can expose personal information or become targets for scams.

options: Use unique passwords and enable MFA
why: Unique passwords limit damage from credential reuse, and MFA adds another barrier.

q: Which detail should make you inspect an email more carefully?
options: Unexpected attachment and a login link
A saved contact with no request
why: Unexpected attachments and login prompts deserve careful verification.

q: Why should you pause before posting a personal photo with location clues?
options: Location clues can reveal where you are
why: Background details can reveal places, routines or other identifying information.

q: You receive a frightening family-emergency video request for money. What should you do?
options: Call the person using a known number and verify
why: Deepfake audio/video can be convincing; independent verification is important.

q: A bank message asks you to click a shortened link and enter your PIN. What should you do?
options: Open the bank app or official site directly
why: Use a known official route rather than links in unexpected messages.

q: In India, what is the cybercrime helpline for immediate reporting of cyber financial fraud?
why: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal states 1930 is the helpline for immediate reporting of cyber financial fraud.

q: Where can people submit online cybercrime complaints in India?
why: The Government of India portal at cybercrime.gov.in is designed to facilitate cybercrime complaints.

q: A group chat is distracting you while studying. What can help?
why: Notification controls can reduce distraction without requiring unsafe account sharing.

q: Why should you avoid reusing the same password across work and personal accounts?
options: A stolen password may unlock more than one account
why: Password reuse creates credential-stuffing risk across services.
